That page's Back link carries only ?type= and no template id, so a user who has typed a name but not saved it goes back to the question without a template. Continuing again then lands on an empty /templates/new, and SCN-INS-NTYPE-004-E correctly says nothing is stored. The round trip the gap describes happens only after the name has been saved. The user reaches Origin of the import, follows Back to /templates/<id>/name (origin/controller.js:59), then follows Back to /notification-type/template?type=..&template=<id> (type-question-url.js). From there, Continue, including after the empty-choice error, which keeps the id in a hidden field, goes to /templates/<id>/name?type=.. with the saved name. Choosing Germinal products shows that type on the name page; saving it redirects to Manage templates. A type that templates cannot have, such as potatoes, is ignored when the question is shown again (valuesOf(TEMPLATE_TYPES)). SCN-TEMPLATES-005-D covers only Origin -> Back -> name page. SCN-TEMPLATES-005-B and SCN-INS-NTYPE-004-D cover only Back to the question. No scenario covers continuing again, so the gap is real once its starting point is corrected. Leave out the potatoes pre-select detail: a user can reach it only by editing the URL, so it is not worth a scenario.

eng.title: The templates merge resolutions
eng.summary:
I checked the three conflicted merges (animals frontend 74d79f1f, INS frontend 340e956, tests 17fa81c) against both parents, plus the backend and plants merges, which went through cleanly. Nothing was lost from either side:

- **Shared save-actions macro:** it combines the template change, amend and hub-exit endings correctly. Template change wins, then amend, then the default. Only the template change ending has no hub exit or formaction. Every page that passed `amend` before the merge now also passes `templateChange` by name. The pickers, CPH number and transporter-add pages correctly pass neither.
- **Review controller split:** the notification review is byte-for-byte the combined side's. The template review keeps all of templates' behaviour: its title, Save template, no errors, Back to the task list, and no Delete or Cancel amend.
- **`changeReturnPath`:** wiring this into `exitTarget` and the addresses Back link keeps the amend rule. Every page still saves through `nextTarget`, so a change to a saved template returns to its page and the "updated" banner still shows.
- **Commodity save and Back link:** these keep templates' AC, and HEAD behaviour is unchanged outside template mode.
- **Review partial:** `_review-sections.njk`, rebuilt on the combined card markup, renders the same cards on the template review and the saved-template page.
- **Tests repo:** the page-object clean-up, the `journeyStripTag` rename and the renamed spec strings did not weaken any absence check. `summaryCard` now matches the exact title, and 'Document 1' and 'Identification details' are names the combined branch really renders.
- **INS frontend:** removing the `pageTitle` override is a no-op.

There is one real defect from the merge: the template review and saved-template page headings were frozen in copy, so the combined branch's section rename did not reach them. There is one weakened unit test, and one low risk in the merged surface outside the conflict hunks (a GET that creates a draft).

The merge introduced this: the merge kept the frozen copy instead of deriving the heading.

survived.title: Template review unit test's 'no card errors' check is vacuous: it reads `card.errorMessage`, which no card has
survived.what: The merged template-review describe asserts `cardsOf(context.sections).filter((card) => card.errorMessage)` equals `[]`. On the combined markup (and already on the templates side), a card's error is `card.error`, set by `withCardErrors` in incomplete-cards.js:164, and a section's error is `section.error`. Nothing in check-answers sets `errorMessage`, so the filter always returns `[]`. The template-mode part of `holdsSilently` in the merged controller, which suppresses card errors, has no card-level unit coverage. Only the `errorSummary` null check guards it.
survived.scenario: Remove `inTemplateMode() ||` from `holdsSilently` in check-answers/controller.js. An unanswered template review then gets 'Complete origin of import' and similar errors on its cards. The `errorSummary` toBeNull assertion catches that today, but the card-level assertion would pass either way. A later change that keeps the summary empty but marks cards would slip through.
survived.fix: Assert on the real fields: no card has `error` and no section has `error` (`expect(cardsOf(context.sections).filter((card) => card.error)).toEqual([])` and the same over `context.sections`). That makes the check fail when card errors return in template mode.
survived.verifierNote: I confirmed this one. check-answers.test.js:2725 filters cards on `card.errorMessage`, and that field appears nowhere else in check-answers. Cards carry `error` (incomplete-cards.js:161-164), so the filter always returns [] and the 'no card errors' half of the test is vacuous. The suppression comes from `inTemplateMode()` in holdsSilently (controller.js:221), and only the errorSummary toBeNull assertion guards it. The test came in with the templates surface (cab954f8), not a conflict hunk, but it is part of the merged diff. This is a test-coverage gap only, not a runtime defect.

survived.title: GET /start creates a draft notification on any signed-in request (outside the conflict hunks, merged into the combined dashboard controller)
survived.what: `startGet` is registered on `GET /start` and runs `openNewNotification`. That calls `startJourney`, which creates and persists a draft through `records.create`, then `beginOpeningRun`. No crumb or confirmation step is involved. The backlog's own rule (c-309, restated in the notes of inc-157, inc-158 and inc-160) is that every state change is a form post. This route breaks that rule so that the INS type question can hand over cross-origin. Plants' dashboard gained the same route in the same merge.
survived.scenario: While signed in, a trader opens any page that links to /live-animals/start, or a link preview or prefetch fetches it. Lax cookies are sent on top-level GET navigation, so each fetch stores a new empty GBN-AG draft. The draft then appears on the dashboard and needs deleting.
survived.fix: Make /start idempotent and free of side effects. Render a GOV.UK confirmation page with its own crumb'd form post that creates the draft. Alternatively, have the INS type question hand over a short-lived signed token, and check it before creating anything. Apply the same change to plants' /start.
survived.verifierNote: The scenario holds. dashboard/controller.js:131-157 registers GET /start, which runs openNewNotification (startJourney followed by beginOpeningRun) and creates a draft with no crumb. The merge added this route (it is not in HEAD^1). The auth cookie is SameSite=Lax (config.js:19, auth.js:69), so a top-level cross-site GET or a prefetch carries the session and creates an empty draft. Two caveats lower the severity. First, it is a deliberate inc-148 design choice, documented in the code comment and backlog.json:182: a cross-origin POST cannot carry the crumb. It sat behind a human design gate (line 187). Second, the finding overstates c-309. In the backlog, c-309 covers storing and using templates through form posts, not every state change. The only impact is an unwanted empty draft, with no data exposure. This is not a merge-resolution defect, but it is real in the merged surface.

eng.title: Animals backend: templates (#106)
eng.summary:
Animals backend templates package (#106, 9 commits merged cleanly into the combined branch). Per-user scoping holds. Every read and write goes through findByIdAndOwnerId or findAllByOwnerId, and another user's template answers 404. No path writes a template to the outbox, to SNS or to PIMS: it uses its own notification_templates collection with no Mongo event listeners or change streams. Six findings, none critical:
1. Medium: the updates are read-modify-write with a version the client never sends. A double-clicked Save returns a 409 even though the template was saved, and two tabs silently overwrite each other's answers.
2. Medium: the ownership tests are thin. The cross-user ITs cover GET and save only, and the service unit test mocks the repository.
3. Low to medium: the identity model is a single trusted User-Id header, with organisationId recorded but never used.
4. Low: POST /{id}/save is an action path, against the noun-endpoint rule.
5. Low: GET /templates is unbounded. It has no paging and returns every template's full answers.
6. Low: there is dead "legacy row" handling and wording for rows that cannot exist. A null-status row also bypasses the in-progress check.
Not reported: delete and discard, because they are unbuilt rows inc-164 and inc-165.

survived.title: Template updates are read-modify-write with a server-only version: a double-clicked Save returns 409 and two tabs silently overwrite each other
survived.what: updateDetails, replaceFulfilments and save each call load() (findByIdAndOwnerId), change the entity and then call repository.save(). @Version is on the entity, but the frontend client (services/templates/client.js) never sends the version back, and no endpoint accepts an expected version. The only concurrency check is whether two requests overlap inside the backend. Overlapping requests get an OptimisticLockingFailureException, which the global handler turns into 409 STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN. Requests that do not overlap silently overwrite each other, because PUT /fulfilments replaces the whole list.
survived.scenario: (a) The user double-clicks 'Save template' on the review page. Two POST /templates/{id}/save requests both load version 3. The first writes version 4. The second gets a 409, and the frontend's failed() throws a BackendRequestError, so the user sees an error page even though the template was saved. (b) The user opens a saved template in two tabs. Tab A changes origin, then tab B changes the consignee. Tab B's PUT /fulfilments sends the full answer list it read before A's change, so A's origin change is lost and no error is shown.
survived.fix: Make save idempotent and atomic. Use MongoTemplate.findAndModify with Criteria where(_id).is(id).and(ownerId).is(ownerId), and Update set(status, SAVED), so a repeated save is a no-op instead of a 409. Set 'saved' with a separate conditional update (criteria saved: null) or $min. For replaceFulfilments and updateDetails, accept the expected version (a concurrencyToken, as notifications use) and match on it, returning 409 when it is stale. Have the frontend send back the version it read and handle the 409 as notifications already do.
survived.verifierNote: Holds on the branch. NotificationTemplateService.save, replaceFulfilments and updateDetails all call load() and then repository.save() on an entity that carries @Version. The frontend client (services/templates/client.js) sends no version, and no endpoint accepts one. GlobalExceptionHandler maps OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409, and check-answers saveTemplate (controller.js:286) has no catch, so an overlapping save shows an error page. The template-records port sends the full fulfilment set it loaded earlier, so the two-tab lost update is real. Three things lower the severity. Notifications' own fulfilment replace has no expected-version check either (only /copy takes a concurrencyToken), so this copies the house pattern rather than falling short of it. A double-click gap (around 100ms) is usually longer than one Mongo find-and-save, so the second save normally runs after the first and leaves the template saved. And a lost update needs the same user editing in two tabs.

survived.title: The ownership boundary on PUT /details and PUT /fulfilments is only proven through a mocked repository
survived.what: The ITs test cross-user access only for GET /templates/{id} and POST /templates/{id}/save. Nothing over HTTP and Mongo shows that PUT /templates/{id}/details and PUT /templates/{id}/fulfilments return 404 for another user and leave the document unchanged. NotificationTemplateServiceTest mocks NotificationTemplateRepository with Mockito: it stubs findByIdAndOwnerId and verifies save(). That tests which repository method is called rather than the behaviour, and it breaks the house rule to mock only at the network boundary. A refactor to findById plus an owner check, or to a MongoTemplate update that drops the owner criterion, would keep the unit tests green.
survived.scenario: Someone later swaps load() for repository.findById(id) in replaceFulfilments, for example to share code with a future 'use template' path. User B can then overwrite user A's template answers by guessing or leaking a 24-hex id. The unit test with stubbed findByIdAndOwnerId is rewritten alongside the change, and no IT fails. This is the same class of hole as the programme's open 'notifications listed unscoped per user' security ticket.
survived.fix: Add ITs for both PUT routes with OTHER_OWNER: expect 404, then read the row from the repository and assert that setId, name and fulfilments are unchanged. Replace the Mockito-repository service test with the IT, or keep only the parts that need no repository mock (the saved-time rules can be checked through the IT as well).
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. NotificationTemplateIT has cross-owner tests only for GET /{id} (get_shouldReturn404_forAnotherOwnersTemplate) and POST /{id}/save (save_shouldReturn404_forAnotherOwnersTemplate). No IT sends OTHER_OWNER to PUT /details or PUT /fulfilments. NotificationTemplateServiceTest uses a Mockito @Mock repository, stubs findByIdAndOwnerId and verifies save(), which breaks the rule to mock only at the network boundary. Today's code is correct, because every path goes through load(). The gap is regression protection for the ownership boundary.

survived.title: POST /templates/{id}/save is an action path, not a noun endpoint
survived.what: The template API is new and could follow the house REST rule (noun endpoints). /details and /fulfilments are sub-resources, but /save is a verb. It only changes a status field, so it fits the same sub-resource pattern.
survived.scenario: Delete and discard (inc-164 and inc-165) will be added beside this endpoint. The verb style tends to spread into routes such as POST /templates/{id}/discard and POST /templates/{id}/delete, and then the API mixes styles and needs a breaking change to tidy up.
survived.fix: Model it as PUT /templates/{id}/status with body {"status":"SAVED"}, validated so it only accepts the transition from IN_PROGRESS to SAVED. Use DELETE /templates/{id} for the coming delete and discard rows.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed at NotificationTemplateController.java:118: @PostMapping("/{id}/save") is a verb path on a brand-new API, against the house rule for noun endpoints. It is mitigated because the existing backend already has verb paths such as POST /notifications/{ref}/copy, so this is a style point, not a functional defect.

survived.title: GET /templates is unbounded and returns every template's full answers
survived.what: listFor loads every saved template for the owner, with no limit or paging. Each NotificationTemplateSummary carries the complete fulfilments list, which is the whole notification answer payload, so the frontend can summarise cards. Nothing limits the number of templates per user or the size of the fulfilments.
survived.scenario: A high-volume importer keeps 200 templates, each holding a full set of commodity, party and transport answers. Every visit to Manage templates pulls all 200 documents and serialises them into one response, which the frontend then decodes. Latency and heap use grow linearly, and a large account can push the backend toward OOM under concurrent load.
survived.fix: Add paging, as notifications already have (page and size, plus totalItems from count). Alternatively, project only the fields the card needs (category, parties' addresses) on the server rather than returning the raw fulfilments. Consider a per-user cap on templates.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. listFor calls findAllByOwnerIdAndStatusNotOrderBySavedDescCreatedDesc with no Pageable and no limit. NotificationTemplateSummary carries the full fulfilments, and the frontend Manage templates page decodes every one through cardAnswersFor. Notifications have paging and templates do not. The impact is speculative at expected per-user volumes, so the severity is low.

survived.title: Dead 'legacy row' handling and migration-style wording for null-status rows that cannot exist; such a row also bypasses the in-progress guard
survived.what: The whole template package arrives in this merge, and no environment has notification_templates rows. Even so, the Javadoc ('Rows written before templates could be created carry none and read as saved', 'or on a row saved before this was recorded') and the code (NotificationTemplateResponse.from treats a null status as SAVED, listFor's status-not-IN_PROGRESS filter lets null through, replaceFulfilments treats null as saved, and the sort orders by saved then created to place legacy rows) cater for rows from earlier increments on the same unmerged branch. That breaks the 'no migration comments' rule. It also means any row inserted without a status, for example by a raw seed or a future write path that forgets to set it, is listed and usable as a saved template.
survived.scenario: The IT seed() helper already inserts rows with no status, and they appear on Manage templates as saved. A future write path that builds a NotificationTemplate without .status(...) would quietly publish a half-made template to the user's list and let it start notifications.
survived.fix: Make status required: give it a @Builder.Default of IN_PROGRESS and drop the null branches. Have listFor query status == SAVED. Sort by saved descending only, or by (saved, _id). Remove the legacy wording from the Javadoc and the Schema descriptions, and make the IT seed() set status SAVED and saved explicitly.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed. The whole template package is new in this merge (git log origin/main shows no history for it), and no seed in the tests repo or the frontend writes notification_templates, so no environment holds rows without a status. Even so, the NotificationTemplate Javadoc (lines 55-56 and 61-64) describes rows 'written before templates could be created' and 'saved before this was recorded'. The service Javadoc at line 17 says the same. NotificationTemplateResponse.from maps a null status to SAVED. The StatusNot(IN_PROGRESS) query lets a null status through, and the IT findAll_shouldStillListARowWithNoStatus seeds a 'Legacy' row to pin that behaviour. This is migration-style wording and handling, which the house rules ban. It also means a row written without a status shows up in the list as a saved template.

killed.title: Ownership rests entirely on a caller-asserted User-Id header, and organisationId is stored but never used
killed.what: The backend takes User-Id as the owner without verifying it. Its only checks are @NotBlank and nothing else. Any caller that can reach the backend inside CDP can read, change or save any user's templates by setting the header. organisationId is stored on start (it is optional and has no validation) but is never used to scope, so a user's templates follow them across organisations. Templates hold party answers, including addresses from the organisation-scoped address book. The frontend side is also loose: client.js puts ownerId into the header straight from buildActor(request.auth?.credentials)?.id. If that is undefined, fetch sends the literal string 'undefined', which passes @NotBlank, so every user without an id would share one owner bucket.
killed.scenario: (a) A user who belongs to two organisations in Defra ID saves a template under organisation A, with A's consignee and importer addresses, then switches to organisation B. Manage templates still lists the template. Using it starts a B notification pre-filled with A's address-book parties. (b) A session that resolves to no actor id lists, and saves into, the templates of every other session with no actor id, all under owner 'undefined'.
killed.fix: Decide explicitly whether templates are scoped by user only or by user and organisation. The backlog says 'or user, for templates', but the multi-organisation case is not covered. If organisation matters, make organisationId required and part of every query and of the compound index. Reject User-Id values that are not a valid actor-id shape. In the frontend, refuse to call the API when ownerId is missing rather than sending it. Record the trusted-header model alongside the existing notifications security ticket.
killed.refutation: Refuted as a defect in this merge. (1) The 'undefined' owner scenario cannot happen: services/templates/index.js requireOwner() throws before every client call (listFor, startFor, getFor, updateDetailsFor, replaceFulfilmentsFor, saveFor) when ownerId is falsy, so the literal string 'undefined' is never sent. (2) A trusted User-Id header is the backend's existing model: NotificationController already takes HEADER_USER_ID as a required header at lines 225 and 258 without verifying it. The templates merge did not introduce it. (3) Scoping templates by user, not organisation, is the stated intent. The backlog constraint (backlog.json line 39) reads 'scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates)', and the field's Javadoc says organisationId is 'Recorded, not used to scope'. The multi-organisation case is a product question, not a bug.

eng.title: Workspace tooling changed on laptop 2
eng.summary:
The five laptop-2 commits make long gates work, mostly correctly: gate-wait waits in slices, results are written atomically, the parallelRepos worker pool is right, and stackAfterLocal holds the lease and stack refresh until layer one finishes. Three real risks remain, all in waiting on a long gate.
1. A result file carries nothing that says which gate run wrote it, and two gates for the same holder are not stopped from running at once. A gate the agent gave up on keeps running, and its result can land in the next gate's file and be read as that gate's verdict, possibly green on untested code.
2. gate-wait cannot tell a crashed gate from a slow one. A gate killed by memory pressure or a tool kill costs up to about 3h10m of waiting before anyone calls it red.
3. The lease teardown found this morning (a gate that finds the run's stack down restarts it under the run's own holder, then releases it at the end) is not fixed by these commits. stackAfterLocal makes the window for it bigger.
Also lower: 664beddd stopped writing (or clearing) a result when argument checks or workspace lookup fail, and the help, plain-text report and docs still say repos run at the same time and the stack gets ready during layer one. Test quality is mostly in line with tim/CLAUDE.md (input and output, no spies), but nothing tests a dead or overlapping gate, a cap between 1 and N, or the refresh path with a reused lease.

survived.title: A result file does not say which gate run wrote it, so a leftover gate's result is read as the current one
survived.what: The gate clears gate-result-<phase>.json once, when it starts, and writes it when it ends. gate-wait returns whatever file appears at that path. Nothing ties a result to the run that is being waited on: no pid, no start-time token, no lock on the logs folder. Stages that repeat reuse one folder: the ladder always writes to logs/<id>-ladder, fix rounds to logs/<id>-fix, and recoverDownStack reruns a stage into the same folder. GATE_WAIT_RULE tells the agent to report "the gate did not finish" as red after 20 waits but never to stop the gate, so that gate keeps running.
survived.scenario: With parallelRepos 1 over five repos, the ladder gate runs past the 600s call plus 20 × 540s waits, about 3h10m. The agent reports it red as "did not finish" and the loop moves to fix. The fix stage's unit and FIT gate runs beside the leftover ladder gate. That is two gates at once, which the parallelRepos cap exists to stop. Its FIT rungs go red with "Port N is in use" from the leftover gate's FIT server. The next ladder clears gate-result-all.json and starts. The leftover gate then finishes and renames its envelope into that same path, and the new ladder's gate-wait returns it straight away. That result came from the code as it was before the fix. If it is green, the loop treats code it never tested as green. Both gates also share the run's holder, so both refresh or rebuild the same stack services at once.
survived.fix: Give each gate run an identity. When it clears the result, write gate-running-<phase>.json with its pid and a nonce, put the nonce in the result envelope, and have gate-wait return only a result whose nonce matches the marker that was there when the wait began. Also make tim build gate refuse to start while another gate's marker in the same folder names a live pid, or take a machine-wide gate lock, because the parallelRepos cap only applies within one process. Change GATE_WAIT_RULE so a gate that runs out of waits is stopped (by pid, from the marker), not left running.
survived.verifierNote: Holds on the branch. gate-result.js waitForGateResult (lines 55-67) returns any envelope at the path. index.js:328 clears it once at start and :338 writes it at the end, with no run token, pid or lock. increment-build-loop.js:947-960 gives a fixed path per logs folder (gateResultFile) and has GATE_WAIT_RULE report 'the gate did not finish' after MAX_GATE_WAITS=20 without stopping the gate. gates.json now sets parallelRepos 1, and the loop's own comment at :950 says a one-repo-at-a-time gate over five repos runs well past 1.5h. That makes a gate outrunning about 3h10m plausible. A later gate in the same folder (the ladder reruns into logs/<id>-ladder) can then get the leftover gate's envelope. Severity is below high: it needs a gate that runs past the full wait budget, and it needs the backgrounded Bash process to outlive the stage agent that started it, which I could not show for certain.

survived.title: gate-wait cannot tell a dead gate from a slow one, so a crashed gate costs up to about 3 hours
survived.what: waitForGateResult only checks whether the result file exists. A gate killed by the OS or the tool (SIGKILL from memory pressure on the 16 GB laptop these commits are about, or a Bash tool that kills rather than backgrounds on timeout) writes no result. The catch block that writes an error envelope runs only for thrown errors, not for signals.
survived.scenario: A five-repo baseline's mvn verify and FIT suites push the laptop into memory pressure and the tim node process is killed. The agent gets GATE_STILL_RUNNING 20 times, about 3 hours, before reporting "the gate did not finish". Meanwhile no gate is running. If it was killed after the stack started, the stack is left up under the lease.
survived.fix: Have the gate write a marker with its pid when it starts (the same marker as GATE-1). Have gate-wait check that the pid is still alive (process.kill(pid, 0)) on each poll, and return a distinct GATE_DIED error at once when the process has gone and there is no result. Add a test that spawns a gate, kills it, and asserts that gate-wait reports it dead instead of still running.
survived.verifierNote: waitForGateResult only polls for the file. Nothing in gate-result.js or index.js records a pid or checks that the gate process is alive. The catch at index.js:343 runs only on thrown errors, so a SIGKILL of the tim node process writes nothing, and gate-wait answers GATE_STILL_RUNNING until the agent's 20 waits are used up. I rate it low: memory pressure is more likely to kill the large java or chromium children, which tim sees as a red rung, than the tim node parent. The loop's rule also moves a timed-out call to the background instead of killing it.

survived.title: The gate can still tear down the run's own lease, and stackAfterLocal makes the window for it bigger
survived.what: None of the five commits changes takeLease or giveBack. acquireDecision still returns 'start' for the same holder when the stack is down, and runE2e still calls giveBack whenever lease.started. If a gate run under the run's holder finds the run's stack down, it starts the stack, then stops it and clears the run's lease. 0ff6e2f4 adds `if (context.stackAfterLocal) await context.localDone` before takeLease, and gates.json now sets stackAfterLocal true. The lease is therefore checked only after layer one, which with parallelRepos 1 can take well over an hour.
survived.scenario: The run holds the lease and the stack is up. During the ladder's 90-minute one-repo-at-a-time layer one, Docker Desktop restarts and the stack goes down. Before these commits the gate checked the lease when it started. Now it checks only after layer one. It finds its own holder with the stack down, starts the stack (started=true), runs E2E, then releases: it stops the stack and clears the run's lease. The next stage's lease status shows no lease and returns stackHeld with holder null, which stops the loop, or the run's own release at the end finds nothing to release.
survived.fix: In runE2e, when the holder is a build-run holder that already had a lease (the lease existed for this holder before acquire), never give it back: leave the stack up and the lease in place, and report startedForE2e so the loop knows. Or refuse with a 'stackDown' result so recoverDownStack takes the lease again properly. Add a gate.test case: a lease held by the same holder, the stack down, phase all. Assert that the lease file still names the holder and that stop-stack.sh was not called.
survived.verifierNote: stack-lease.js acquireDecision line 146: for the same holder, `if (!up) return 'start'`. acquireStack then calls startUnderLease (started:true), and gate.js:453 calls giveBack whenever lease.started, which stops the stack and clears the run's own lease. The bug is older than these commits and none of them changes it. gate.js:438 (`if (context.stackAfterLocal) await context.localDone`), together with gates.json stackAfterLocal true and parallelRepos 1, moves the lease check to after a long one-repo-at-a-time layer one, so the stack has more time to go down unseen. The likely outcome is that the loop stops on stackHeld with holder null. Code under test is not mistaken for green.

survived.title: Help text, plain-text report and docs still say repos run at the same time and the stack gets ready during layer one
survived.what: gates.json now sets parallelRepos 1 and stackAfterLocal true. The gate's --help still says "The stack gets ready during the first layer". describeTiming prints "unit and FIT first, repos at the same time" in every plain-text report. The runGate JSDoc and the comment above FLAKY_COUNT in gate.js say the same. The README baseline row that 05ecdb98 edited still says "unit, FIT and E2E side by side".
survived.scenario: Someone reading a slow baseline's text report, or the README, expects repos to run in parallel and the stack to come up early. They look for a hang or starvation bug that is really the configured one-at-a-time order. Readers of the user-facing strings are told something that is no longer true.
survived.fix: Make describeTiming and the --help text depend on parallelRepos and stackAfterLocal (put both in the outcome so the report can say "one repo at a time, stack readied after"). Update the runGate JSDoc and the README baseline row to match.
survived.verifierNote: The stale text is all there. describeTiming at index.js:156 always prints 'unit and FIT first, repos at the same time'. The --help at index.js:301 still says 'The stack gets ready during the first layer', without mentioning stackAfterLocal. The comments at gate.js:371-373 and :487-490 and the runGate JSDoc at :546-550 say the stack gets ready during or beside layer one. gates.json now sets parallelRepos 1 and stackAfterLocal true. The README line cited in the finding did not show up in tim/README.md (its only 'side by side' match is unrelated), so that part is unverified. This affects docs only.

survived.title: Concurrency tests leave out the cap between 1 and N and the refresh path with a reused lease
survived.what: The new tests prove that parallelRepos 1 runs strictly one repo at a time, and that stackAfterLocal starts a stack that was down only after the unit rung. Nothing covers a cap of 2 of 3 repos: at most two overlapping, the third starting once the first finishes, results still in plan order. That is the setting ced1a1a3 shipped. Nothing covers stackAfterLocal on the build loop's real path, where the holder already leases the stack, so refreshLeasedStack, not run-stack.sh, is what has to wait for layer one.
survived.scenario: A later change to runChainsAtMost (for example a worker that takes its next chain before the last one finishes, or limit handling that drops to all chains when limit > 1) or to where refresh is called breaks the 16 GB laptop protection. Every existing test still passes, and the baseline goes red on timeouts again.
survived.fix: Add a timeline test with parallelRepos 2 and three repos. Assert the largest number of starts without a matching end is 2, and that the results come back in plan order. Add a stackAfterLocal test with a lease seeded for the same holder and the stack up. Assert the rebuild or restart log entry in stack-calls comes after the unit rung's marker.
survived.verifierNote: gate.test.js:793-821 tests only parallelRepos 1 (a strict sequence). :823-847 tests stackAfterLocal only on the cold-start path (run-stack.sh -d then stop-stack.sh) with no lease seeded. No test covers a cap between 1 and N (runChainsAtMost with a limit of 2 or more and fewer than all chains). No test covers stackAfterLocal with a lease already held by the same holder, where refreshLeasedStack is the call that has to wait. Both gaps are real.

killed.title: An argument or workspace-lookup error no longer writes, or clears, the --result file
killed.what: 664beddd moved the result path out of the try block's preamble (`let resultPath = null`) and sets it only after parseOptions and resolveWorkspaceRoot succeed. Before this commit, `--result` was resolved first, so a validation or workspace-root error both cleared the file and wrote an error envelope to it. Now neither happens, and a result left by an earlier run stays in place.
killed.scenario: A stage runs the gate with a holder the regex refuses, or a --workspace that does not resolve. tim exits 2 with no result written, and the gate-result-<phase>.json from the last round is still there. An agent that then follows GATE_WAIT_RULE and calls gate-wait gets the old round's envelope back at once, which may be green, and reports it as this gate's. The existing test 'writes an error to the --result file when the gate cannot start' still passes only because its error is thrown later, from runGate.
killed.fix: Resolve the explicit --result path (resolve(opts.result)) before parseOptions, as 05ecdb98 did, so it is cleared and written on every failure. Fall back to the default path only once logsDir is known. Add a test with an invalid --holder and --result that asserts the file holds ok:false.
killed.refutation: The regression is real. Before 664beddd, `resultPath = opts.result ? resolve(opts.result) : null` came before parseOptions, so a parse or workspace-lookup error wrote an error envelope. Now index.js:309-328 sets resultPath only after both succeed. The harmful scenario does not hold, though. Those errors make the foreground gate call exit 2 at once with the error on stdout. It is never moved to the background, so GATE_WAIT_RULE never sends the agent to gate-wait, and GATE_RULE (increment-build-loop.js:982-983) says an error before any rung is RED. The holder is always the fixed RUN_HOLDER from gateCommand, so the 'regex refuses the holder' trigger cannot come from the loop. Even before the commit, a parse failure never cleared the file. To read a stale envelope, an agent would have to break the loop's rules.

eng.title: Tests repo: templates specs
eng.summary:
The templates merge in the tests repo seeds no journeys. template-parties creates address-book entries through the API, but only as picker set-up, which is the same pattern 10 other specs use. The merge kept the absence checks it retargeted (template review, template page, task list) able to fail, with one exception: the 'Document 1' card check can never fail. Review these hardest:
1. Three tests are built to flake. All 16 workers sign in as Andrew, tests run in parallel, and these tests need Andrew's draft list and template count to stay the same during the test.
2. Two assertions always pass: the one claiming the region code is required, and the one saying a saved template never shows on the dashboard.
3. Most templates specs cross between services and are not tagged @compose, so they run on CDP. The three cross-service navigation specs are @compose-only and do not.

I ran no E2E (the stack is in use), so these findings come from reading the specs, page objects and merged frontend source.

survived.title: Before-and-after comparisons on the shared default user flake under parallel workers
survived.what: Three tests snapshot Andrew's state, act, then expect it unchanged. In create-template.spec.ts: line 83 checks the Manage templates results line still reads the same, and lines 84 and 190 check the draft references on page 1 of the dashboard still match. change-template.spec.ts line 114 makes the same draft-list check. shared-config sets fullyParallel: true, and auth-state signs every worker in as defaultUser (users.andrew). So every other worker's saved template and every live-animals journey spec's new draft lands in the same lists while these tests run.
survived.scenario: Worker 3 is in create-template's 'leaving before the name page is posted adds nothing' test, between reading the 'before' count and the Cancel. At that moment worker 7 runs save-template and worker 9 runs any journey spec that creates a GBN-AG draft. The results line moves from 'Show 1-41 of 41' to 'Show 1-42 of 42', and the newest draft heads the dashboard's page 1. Both assertions fail even though the feature works. The one retry (retries: 1) often hits the same race, so the run goes red or gets labelled flaky.
survived.fix: Run these tests as an identity no other spec writes to, starting cold: browser.newContext({ storageState: COLD_START }) and manageTemplates.open(true, { userId: <dedicated user> }), as manage-templates.spec does for Sarah. Alternatively assert on things this test owns: no request to /live-animals/start or /notifications (already captured at line 191), and no draft whose origin/internal reference carries this test's unique marker. Do not loosen the equality.
survived.verifierNote: Confirmed on the branch. shared-config.ts sets fullyParallel: true and retries: 1. Sign-in with no options falls back to defaultUser = users.andrew (config/users.ts:23, used by base-page and sign-in-page). create-template.spec.ts:72-84 reads Andrew's results line and page-1 draft references, runs a multi-page cross-service flow, then asserts exact equality. Lines 177-190 do the same. Any other worker that saves a template as Andrew (save-template, template-review, view-template, change-template, use-template) or starts a live-animals draft as Andrew in that window changes the results line or the page-1 draft list. dashboard.draftReferences (added by the merge) reads page 1 only. All of this code is new in the merge, and nothing isolates the identity. The same file's requestsToAnimals capture at 179-194 already proves the 'nothing created' intent without shared state.

survived.title: 'Requires the region of origin code' check passes even if that rule is removed
survived.what: The test picks Yes for the region code but never chooses a country. It then asserts only that an error summary shows and the title starts with 'Error:'. Template mode keeps the page's required-answer checks (c-308), so a missing country alone produces both. Nothing ties the error to the region code.
survived.scenario: Someone drops the 'region code required when Yes' check from template mode. Save and continue still fails on the missing country, the error summary still shows, and the test passes. The behaviour its title promises is no longer tested.
survived.fix: Call originOfImport.selectCountry('France') before choosing Yes, as the next test does. Then assert the exact region-code entry, using errorSummaryLinks.filter({ hasText: <region code required message> }) or originOfImport.errorLinkNamed(...), as well as the 'Error:' title.
survived.verifierNote: In origin/validate.js the country is oneOf(countryValues). In run.js a blank choice is an any.only missing answer, which is dropped only when allowMissing is true. The origin controller passes allowMissing only for kit.isHubExit (Save and return), so 'Save and continue' with no country produces a country error by itself. The test at create-template.spec.ts:197-209 never picks a country and asserts only that an error summary shows and the title starts with 'Error:'. It still passes if regionCodeSuffixRule stops requiring the code under Yes. The next test (211-227) shows the right pattern: select France and filter errorSummaryLinks by the exact message.

survived.title: 'Never appears among the user's notifications' can never fail
survived.what: The test looks for the template's name on the dashboard. Dashboard cards show only a GBN-AG reference, commodity, origin, arrival, consignee, consignor and status, and none of these can hold a template name. So even if Save template wrongly created a draft notification, the name would still be absent and the assertion would pass.
survived.scenario: A regression makes saving a template also create a live-animals draft. The new draft appears first on Andrew's dashboard with a GBN-AG reference, getByText(name) still finds nothing, and the test stays green.
survived.fix: Record requests to the animals origin across the save, as create-template's requestsToAnimals does. Then assert none went to /live-animals/start or /live-animals/notifications/*. That holds up under parallel runs, unlike comparing the draft list (see F1). Alternatively, save as a dedicated cold identity and assert its dashboard has no drafts.
survived.verifierNote: save-template.spec.ts:139-146 asserts only that main contains no text matching the template name. In this merge the dashboard controller adds only a GET /start route. Dashboard cards render reference, commodity, origin, arrival, parties and status, and nothing carries a template name. So if saving a template wrongly created or listed a draft, the card would have no name in it and the assertion would still pass. The check cannot fail on the regression its title names.

survived.title: 'Listed first' assertions race with other workers saving templates as the same user
survived.what: Lines 68, 102 and 103 assert that the template this test just saved is the first card on Manage templates. Andrew's template list is shared by every worker, and Manage templates has no pagination, so it lists everything, newest first. Another worker's save that commits between this test's save and the Manage templates render takes first place. The 'Untitled template' case (line 103) is worse: several workers save untitled templates, so this test cannot tell which one is its own.
survived.scenario: Workers 2 and 5 press Save template within the same second. Worker 2's redirect renders after worker 5's save, so worker 5's card is first. firstCardViewLink's href holds worker 5's template id, and worker 2's test fails.
survived.fix: Run the save-template 'from a signed-in session' block as a dedicated cold identity, or assert the order relative to a template this test saved earlier, as the 'of two templates' test does. Also give names a crypto.randomUUID() suffix rather than Date.now() (save-template line 48, view-template line 54, template-review), as change-template and use-template already do. templateCard(name) uses exact matching, so a same-millisecond collision between workers breaks strict mode.
survived.verifierNote: save-template.spec.ts:68, 102 and 103 assert that the first card on Manage templates is this test's template, or that the first title is 'Untitled template'. Andrew's template list is shared by every parallel worker signed in as defaultUser, and several specs added in this merge save templates as Andrew. A save that commits between this test's save and the Manage templates render takes first place. For the untitled case, another worker's untitled save makes the test unable to tell which card is its own. The 'of two templates' test (124-137) uses relative order and is safe. The Date.now() name collision point is real but very unlikely. The main race holds.

survived.title: Cross-service templates specs run on CDP, while the matching navigation specs are compose-only
survived.what: The INS templates-navigation, INS use-template and plants templates-navigation specs are tagged @compose. `npm test` (CDP) excludes them, following the precedent of address-book-navigation and cross-service-sessions. Every animals templates spec, though, crosses animals to INS (the type question) and back, and notification-type.spec crosses INS to animals and plants. None of those is tagged @compose, so they all run on CDP. Either the cross-service hop works on CDP, and three specs lose CDP coverage for no reason, or it does not, and about 60 templates and type-question tests will fail on CDP. Sam's rule is that a test behaves the same on both environments.
survived.scenario: A CDP run (`npm test`) executes create-template's beforeEach: Create new template leaves the animals origin for INS's /notification-type/template. If the cross-service session hop that keeps the navigation specs compose-only fails on CDP, every templates spec fails in beforeEach. If it works, the Templates and Use template links that start the templates flow from INS and plants are never checked on CDP.
survived.fix: Decide one way for the cross-service hop. Either remove @compose from the three navigation specs, since the templates specs show the hop is expected to work on CDP, or confirm on CDP that the hop fails and tag the templates and type-question specs to match. Record the reason either way.
survived.verifierNote: The tag split is inconsistent. The INS templates-navigation, INS use-template and plants templates-navigation specs (added in this merge, commits 17038b3 and b9adef9) are tagged @compose, so `npm test` (grep-invert '@compose') skips them on CDP. Meanwhile create-template, save-template, template-review and the other animals templates specs, the animals templates-navigation spec and notification-type.spec are tagged only @integration and make the same animals-to-INS or INS-to-animals/plants hop, using the same waitForURL-on-origin-change plus completeSignInIfRequested pattern. Neither the merge log nor the ruling gives a reason for the difference, and the existing precedent (address-book-navigation, cross-service-sessions) is also unexplained. One of the two groups is tagged wrongly for CDP.

survived.title: Origin template-mode absence checks miss a plain 'Save and return' button
survived.what: originOfImport.btnSaveAndReturn matches 'Save and return to overview' by substring, so toHaveCount(0) here and at template-review.spec.ts line 129 cannot see the plain 'Save and return' button that change mode renders. The change-template spec checks the full button list with submitButtons, but the create flow and the review's Change flow do not.
survived.scenario: Template creation's origin page starts showing the change-mode 'Save and return' button, for example because the ?change flag leaks from the review's Change link. Both absence checks still pass, because neither label contains 'Save and return to overview'.
survived.fix: Assert the whole button set, as change-template does: expect(originOfImport.submitButtons).toHaveText(['Save and continue']) in both places.
survived.verifierNote: In origin-of-import-page.ts, btnSaveAndReturn is getByRole('button', { name: 'Save and return to overview' }), a substring and case-insensitive match. A bare 'Save and return' button does not contain that string, so toHaveCount(0) at create-template.spec.ts:148 and template-review.spec.ts:129 cannot detect it. The same merge added btnSaveAndReturnToTemplate (exact) and submitButtons, and the contact-address side of template-review already checks btnSaveAndReturnBare at count 0, so the origin checks are the gap. Low impact.

survived.title: Germinal hand-off test pins the /start URL and passes on a 404
survived.what: The animals frontend has no /germinal-products route yet. The ruling (inc-148 gate) allows the link to land before the set exists, so today the test passes on a 404 page. It checks only the landed pathname, with a non-retrying expect. When the germinal set is built and /start creates a draft and redirects to its first page, the landed path will no longer be /start, and the test will fail even though the hand-off works.
survived.scenario: The germinal theme ships GET /germinal-products/start, which creates a draft and redirects to /germinal-products/notifications/<id>/origin. continueToService resolves on the final URL, so the toBe(`/germinal-products/start`) check fails.
survived.fix: Capture the hand-off request instead: wait for a request whose pathname is `${SET_BASES.germinalProducts}/start` on the animals origin. Keep the check that no /live-animals/ request was made. Do this before the germinal set lands, so the test holds up when it does.
survived.verifierNote: No germinal route exists in the animals frontend source (grep finds only copy and test references), so today the hand-off lands on a 404 and notification-type.spec.ts:158-160 passes on the URL alone, with plain non-retrying expects. continueToService waits only for the origin change and then for load, so the URL read is the final one after any redirect. The live-animals precedent in this merge (dashboard startGet) creates a draft and redirects to the origin page. When germinal follows that shape, the toBe('/germinal-products/start') check will fail even though the hand-off works. This is brittle but correct today, so the severity is low.

killed.title: Retargeted 'no uploaded documents' check (Document 1 card) can never fail
killed.what: The merge changed summaryCard('Uploaded documents') to summaryCard('Document 1'). A 'Document N' card appears only for an uploaded document, and the template under test has none. With no documents, the review shows the documents section with an 'Upload a valid health certificate' error rather than a 'Document 1' card. So the check passes whether or not asTemplateReview removes the documents section. The section-heading list check at line 81 still catches the section, so coverage holds, but this line is dead weight and looks like a guard it is not.
killed.scenario: asTemplateReview stops filtering DOCUMENTS_SECTION_ANCHOR. The 'Document 1' check still passes. Only line 81 fails ('4. Uploaded documents' appears among the headings), and only because the full heading list happens to be checked.
killed.fix: Replace it with an absence check that can fail, on the documents section anchor or heading. For example, assert that main's h2 named '4. Uploaded documents' has count 0, or that #documents-section has count 0 (the anchor notificationView.documentsSectionError already uses). Do not just delete it. The same applies to cardTitled('Identification details') at line 101. It is also vacuous, because Identification details is an h5 inside the commodity card and never a card title. The heading-role check on line 102 is the one that can fail.
killed.refutation: Refuted. view-model/cards/documents.js always renders one 'Document 1' card when nothing is uploaded ('with none uploaded it carries the design's single "Document 1" card reading Not applicable'), and documentsSection is unconditional. The upload-health-certificate error applies only to SUBMITTED_ACTION_REQUIRED journeys, never to a template. So if asTemplateReview (template-review.js) stopped filtering DOCUMENTS_SECTION_ANCHOR, a 'Document 1' card would render and template-review.spec.ts:82 would fail. The merge log says this retarget was chosen for exactly that reason. One side note does hold: cardTitled('Identification details') at line 101 can never fail, because Identification details is the species block's identifier table heading (species-block.js), not a .govuk-summary-card__title. The heading-role check on line 102 is the one that can fail. That is a minor point, not this finding.

eng.title: Frontend shared code changed by templates
eng.summary:
I reviewed the shared code the templates merge changed in the animals, INS and plants frontends. Template mode cannot leak into a real notification. The template wrapper (AsyncLocalStorage) runs only inside the generated /templates handlers. The records port, path builders, journeyStrip, save-actions and base() only switch inside that wrapper. The notification entry guard only matches /notifications/ paths. A template id never joins the known-journeys cookie, and the template records port is scoped to the owner and refuses create, list, finalise, amend, copy and softDelete. Review submit in template mode short-circuits to saveTemplate, and Use template creates its notification outside template mode.

I found 7 real problems:
1. (High) The INS "Add a new address" round trip from a template's party picker strands the user on a 404 and loses the address.
2. (Medium) A new INS CSP form-action setting defaults to localhost and is missing from the cdp-app-config checkout. On CDP, the type question's hand-over can be blocked when it has to bounce through Defra ID sign-in.
3. (Medium) The plants Templates nav link defaults to http://localhost:3000 and is not set in the cdp-app-config checkout.
4. (Medium) A GET on /start creates a draft in animals and plants. That goes against the "every state change is a form post" ruling, and prefetch or cross-site links create stray drafts.
5. (Low) Choosing Germinal products in template creation silently drops the user back on Manage templates.
6. (Low) Lighthouse never audits a template-mode page.
7. (Low) Template saves drop the concurrency token, so the last save wins without warning.

Note: the cdp-app-config checkout used for findings 2 and 3 was last committed on 28 Sep, so check the live repo before acting on those two.

survived.title: Add a new address from a template's party picker returns to a notification URL and 404s, losing the address
survived.what: templateModeRoutes (src/server/app/shared/template-mode.js:123) twins every party picker under /templates. In template mode the picker still builds the INS add-address link with buildInsAddAddressUrl(request, h, journey.journeyId, party), where journeyId is the template id (ins-handshake.js:48). INS always builds the return URL as <animals>/live-animals/notifications/{notification-id}/address-return (trade-imports-ins-frontend src/server/app/features/address-book/journey-registry.js:9). The return therefore lands on the notification route, outside template mode. currentJourney then calls the notification records port with a template id. Templates live in the separate notification_templates collection, so the load misses and Boom.notFound is thrown. The /templates/{journeyId}/address-return twin exists but nothing ever reaches it.
survived.scenario: Outside stub mode, the trader creates or changes a template, opens Roles and addresses, then Consignor, then 'Add a new address'. They add the address in INS and are redirected to /live-animals/notifications/<templateId>/address-return?..., which shows a 404. The address never reaches the template, the handshake token cookie is left behind, and the trader is off the template journey with no way back except the nav. inc-161 makes party addresses part of a template, so this path is in scope.
survived.fix: Carry the mode through the handshake. Either add a return-kind parameter (for example 'return-to=template') that INS's journey-registry maps to /live-animals/templates/{id}/address-return, or have the animals frontend pass INS a full return path that INS allow-lists. As a stop-gap, hide the 'Add a new address' link while inTemplateMode(). Add a template-mode fit or E2E test for the add-address round trip, which would catch this with the stub off.
survived.verifierNote: Holds. TEMPLATE_MODE_EXCLUDED_SLUGS leaves out only documents, declaration, confirmation, amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete, so templateModeRoutes twins every party picker under /templates/{journeyId}/<party-slug>. party-picker.controller.js:82-83 builds the link with buildInsAddAddressUrl(request, h, journey.journeyId, party) whenever stub mode is off, and in template mode journeyId is the template id. INS journey-registry.js:8-9 hard-codes the return as /notifications/{notification-id}/address-return. That route runs outside template mode. state.commit then loads the id through the notification records port, finds nothing, and currentJourney throws Boom.notFound (engine/journey.js:129-131). Nothing reaches the /templates/{journeyId}/address-return twin. The merge introduced the twinning. I rated it below high because the new address is still saved in the org's address book: the trader can get back to the template from the Templates nav and pick it. The template is not updated, though, and the handshake cookie is left behind.

survived.title: INS CSP form-action falls back to localhost:3007 and the env key is not in the cdp-app-config checkout
survived.what: defraId.formActionOrigins defaults to ['http://localhost:3007'], and content-security-policy.js:13 adds it to form-action. The comment says it exists because the type question's form POST redirects to the animals or plants /start, which redirects again to Defra ID when that frontend has no session. Browsers check form-action on every redirect hop. The local cdp-app-config checkout (services/trade-imports-ins-frontend/{dev,test}, last commit 28 Sep) has no DEFRA_ID_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS. Unless it is set, CDP gets a form-action that allows localhost and not the real Defra ID origin.
survived.scenario: On CDP dev or test, a trader signed in to INS but not yet to the animals frontend chooses 'Live animals' on 'What are you importing?' and presses Continue. The POST 302s to animals /live-animals/start, which 302s to the Defra ID authorize URL. The browser blocks the navigation under form-action, so the trader sees nothing happen or a blocked-navigation error. The same applies to the plants types. Production CSP also advertises http://localhost:3007.
survived.fix: Add DEFRA_ID_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS (the browser-facing Defra ID origin) to every INS cdp-app-config environment. Per the CDP rule, draft it locally and Sam commits. Consider defaulting to [] outside local development, and set the localhost value in docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml, so a missing env value fails safe instead of shipping localhost.
survived.verifierNote: Holds. The merge added defraId.formActionOrigins to INS config.js:204-209 with the default ['http://localhost:3007'] and spread it into CSP formAction (content-security-policy.js:31-35). The notification-type controller answers a form POST with a redirect to the journey frontend's /start (controller.js:106). If that frontend has no session, it redirects again to Defra ID, and form-action is checked at each redirect hop. In the local cdp-app-config checkout (last commit 28 Sep 2026), the INS dev env sets DEFRA_ID_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL to the trade-imports-defra-id-stub.dev.cdp-int.defra.cloud host but has no DEFRA_ID_FORM_ACTION_ORIGINS. On CDP the policy therefore allows localhost:3007 and not the stub or Defra ID origin. Check the live cdp-app-config before acting.

survived.title: Plants Templates nav item links to http://localhost:3000 unless TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL is set in CDP
survived.what: The new tradeImportsAnimalsFrontend.baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:3000, and context.js builds templatesUrl from it for every plants page's service navigation. Only the workspace stack sets TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL (docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:119). The cdp-app-config checkout has it for the INS frontend but not for services/trade-imports-plants-frontend.
survived.scenario: On CDP dev or test, any signed-in plants page shows 'Templates' in the service navigation pointing at http://localhost:3000/live-animals/templates. Clicking it fails to connect.
survived.fix: Add TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL=https://trade-imports-animals-frontend.<env>.cdp-int.defra.cloud to each plants environment in cdp-app-config. Sam commits it. Ship the config before or with the merge.
survived.verifierNote: Holds. The merge added tradeImportsAnimalsFrontend.baseUrl to plants config.js (default http://localhost:3000, env TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL). context.js puts templatesUrl into every page's context, and layout.njk:45 uses it as the Templates nav href. The cdp-app-config checkout's plants dev env (a real deployment with auth enabled) has no TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_FRONTEND_URL. It is also missing TRADE_IMPORTS_INS_FRONTEND_URL, so the plants env file is behind on browser-facing URLs generally, but the Templates link is a new break. The checkout is from 28 Sep, so check the live repo.

survived.title: GET /start creates a notification draft in animals and plants, against the 'every state change is a form post' ruling
survived.what: startGet (in the animals frontend and in the plants dashboard controller) creates a draft, adds it to the known-journeys cookie and begins the opening run on a plain GET, with no crumb or hand-off token. The 9 October afternoon ruling (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm.md:199) says every state change is a form post. A GET with side effects is also triggered by things that never meant to create anything.
survived.scenario: Several things each mint a new empty draft in the trader's list: a link to <animals>/live-animals/start from any site (top-level navigation carries the Lax or Strict same-site session cookie within cdp-int.defra.cloud), browser prefetch or prerender of a typed or suggested URL, a link-preview bot running in the user's session, and a refresh of /start. inc-148's own AC says abandoning the question leaves no empty draft, which these paths break.
survived.fix: Have INS hand over with a short-lived signed hand-off token, as the address-book handshake does: INS mints an HMAC'd nonce, and /start creates the draft only when the token verifies and has not been used. Or make /start render a one-button, crumb-protected 'Continue' form that POSTs to the existing create route. Either way, an unauthenticated-intent GET no longer writes.
survived.verifierNote: Holds. The merge added startGet (animals dashboard/controller.js:131-132), which on a plain GET with no crumb or token calls startJourney and beginOpeningRun, the same as createPost. That is deliberate: a comment says a cross-origin POST cannot carry the crumb. A top-level navigation, a refresh, or a prerender of /start each creates a new empty draft owned by the signed-in trader. That goes against the backlog AC that the question leaves no stray draft. The 9 Oct pm ruling's 'every state change is a form post' is mainly about working without JavaScript, but it still applies. The impact is nuisance drafts, not a data leak or a privilege problem, so I rated it low.

survived.title: No template-mode page is ever audited by Lighthouse
survived.what: audit-targets builds its targets from features/index.js allRoutes. The template-mode twins (/templates/{journeyId}, which is the template task list and the saved template page, and every /templates/{journeyId}/<slug>) are generated only in routes-live-animals.js by templateModeRoutes, so they are neither audited nor listed in SKIPPED. The 'stale reason fails the build' guard cannot see them either.
survived.scenario: An accessibility regression on the saved template page or the template review, such as a duplicate h1, an unlabelled Change link or the 'Template' strip, passes the Lighthouse gate, because only /templates, /templates/new and the notification pages are audited.
survived.fix: Feed auditPaths the same route list the server registers: allRoutes plus templateModeRoutes(allRoutes, {excludedSlugs}). Seed a saved template and an in-progress template in the Lighthouse setup, and map /templates/{journeyId}/* to those ids (a FILLED_BY-style map keyed to 'template'). Twins that are not worth auditing go into SKIPPED with reasons.
survived.verifierNote: Holds. scripts/lighthouse/audit-targets.js builds auditPaths and assertTargetsAreCurrent from allRoutes (features/index.js). allRoutes includes the templates controller's own routes (/templates, /templates/new, and /templates/{journeyId}/name in SKIPPED), but not the twins. Those are generated only in routes-live-animals.js:136-140 through templateModeRoutes. So the saved-template page, the template task list and every template-mode page twin are neither audited nor listed in SKIPPED, and the stale-skip guard cannot see them.

killed.title: Choosing Germinal products for a template silently drops the trader back on Manage templates
killed.what: INS offers Germinal products in template creation (destinations.js TEMPLATE_TYPES, offeredForTemplates: true), and the name page accepts it. newPost and namePost then redirect to templatesPath() with nothing stored and no message, because no germinal set exists in this frontend.
killed.scenario: The trader goes Manage templates, Create new template, picks 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)', presses Continue, enters a name and presses Save and continue. They land back on Manage templates with no template and no explanation, and repeating the steps loops. The ruling lets the germinal notification link land before the set exists, but this path discards the user's input without saying so.

killed.title: Template saves drop the concurrency token: last write wins with no stale-action check
killed.what: The records port behind template mode implements replaceFulfilment(journeyId, fulfilment) and ignores the { known, actor } argument that engine/journey.js replaceJourneyFulfilment passes. replaceTemplateFulfilments sends only { fulfilments }, with no version. The page still renders concurrencyToken from the template version, so it looks protected but is not.
killed.scenario: A trader has a saved template's page open in two tabs. They change Origin in tab A, then change Transport in tab B, which was loaded before A's save. Tab B overwrites the whole fulfilment set with its stale copy, A's origin change is lost, and nothing reports a conflict. Notifications in the same situation get the stale-action rejection.
killed.fix: Send known.concurrencyToken as the expected version on PUT .../fulfilments, and have the backend reject a mismatch with the same 409 shape notification saves use. The existing recoverable or stale-action handling in kit then applies to templates too.
killed.refutation: The two-tab scenario does not happen. state.commit (engine/write/commit.js:7) loads the current record fresh on every POST and applies only that page's patch to it. Tab B's Transport save therefore merges onto the stored fulfilment, which already includes tab A's Origin change, and does not overwrite it with a stale copy. Also, replaceJourneyFulfilment prefers the same-request memo (journey.js:147-150), so notification saves send the freshly loaded version, not the tab's rendered token, and would not reject this case either. What the template port drops is protection against a true simultaneous-write race, which is narrow and not the scenario described.

eng.title: Templates feature folders (sample)
eng.summary: I sampled three areas: the animals frontend templates feature folder, the check-answers template-review changes and the INS notification-type feature. ranked.headline: Nothing from the templates merge loses work from either side, and no template-mode code leaks into a real notification. The most serious problem is in the tests: three templates specs compare Andrew's shared draft and template lists before and after an action, so they will fail at random when the 16 parallel workers all sign in as him. Next come two weaknesses in the build tooling, where a result file does not say which gate run wrote it and a gate that finds the run's own stack down can tear down the run's lease. After those come the stale '4. Consignment parties' heading on the template review, a mismatch in which templates specs run on CDP, three assertions that cannot fail, and three missing deployment settings (the INS form-action origin, the plants Templates link and the animals link). The rest are low-risk: a GET that creates a draft, concurrency and paging gaps in the templates backend, stale help text, thin tests and extra comments.

findings.title: Before-and-after comparisons on the shared default user flake under parallel workers
findings.what: Three tests snapshot Andrew's state, act, then expect it unchanged. In create-template.spec.ts: line 83 checks the Manage templates results line still reads the same, and lines 84 and 190 check the draft references on page 1 of the dashboard still match. change-template.spec.ts line 114 makes the same draft-list check. shared-config sets fullyParallel: true, and auth-state signs every worker in as defaultUser (users.andrew). So every other worker's saved template and every live-animals journey spec's new draft lands in the same lists while these tests run.

The results line moves from 'Show 1-41 of 41' to 'Show 1-42 of 42', and the newest draft heads the dashboard's page 1. Both assertions fail even though the feature works. The one retry (retries: 1) often hits the same race, so the run goes red or gets labelled flaky.

Alternatively assert on things this test owns: no request to /live-animals/start or /notifications (already captured at line 191), and no draft whose origin/internal reference carries this test's unique marker. Do not loosen the equality.

Sign-in with no options falls back to defaultUser = users.andrew (config/users.ts:23, used by base-page and sign-in-page). create-template.spec.ts:72-84 reads Andrew's results line and page-1 draft references, runs a multi-page cross-service flow, then asserts exact equality. Lines 177-190 do the same. Any other worker that saves a template as Andrew (save-template, template-review, view-template, change-template, use-template) or starts a live-animals draft as Andrew in that window changes the results line or the page-1 draft list. dashboard.draftReferences (added by the merge) reads page 1 only. All of this code is new in the merge, and nothing isolates the identity. The same file's requestsToAnimals capture at 179-194 already proves the 'nothing created' intent without shared state.

findings.title: A result file does not say which gate run wrote it, so a leftover gate's result is read as the current one
findings.what: The gate clears gate-result-<phase>.json once, when it starts, and writes it when it ends. gate-wait returns whatever file appears at that path. Nothing ties a result to the run that is being waited on: no pid, no start-time token, no lock on the logs folder. Stages that repeat reuse one folder: the ladder always writes to logs/<id>-ladder, fix rounds to logs/<id>-fix, and recoverDownStack reruns a stage into the same folder. GATE_WAIT_RULE tells the agent to report "the gate did not finish" as red after 20 waits but never to stop the gate, so that gate keeps running.
findings.scenario: With parallelRepos 1 over five repos, the ladder gate runs past the 600s call plus 20 × 540s waits, about 3h10m. The agent reports it red as "did not finish" and the loop moves to fix. The fix stage's unit and FIT gate runs beside the leftover ladder gate. That is two gates at once, which the parallelRepos cap exists to stop. Its FIT rungs go red with "Port N is in use" from the leftover gate's FIT server. The next ladder clears gate-result-all.json and starts. The leftover gate then finishes and renames its envelope into that same path, and the new ladder's gate-wait returns it straight away. That result came from the code as it was before the fix. If it is green, the loop treats code it never tested as green. Both gates also share the run's holder, so both refresh or rebuild the same stack services at once.
findings.fix: Give each gate run an identity. When it clears the result, write gate-running-<phase>.json with its pid and a nonce, put the nonce in the result envelope, and have gate-wait return only a result whose nonce matches the marker that was there when the wait began. Also make tim build gate refuse to start while another gate's marker in the same folder names a live pid, or take a machine-wide gate lock, because the parallelRepos cap only applies within one process. Change GATE_WAIT_RULE so a gate that runs out of waits is stopped (by pid, from the marker), not left running.
findings.verifierNote: Holds on the branch. gate-result.js waitForGateResult (lines 55-67) returns any envelope at the path. index.js:328 clears it once at start and :338 writes it at the end, with no run token, pid or lock. increment-build-loop.js:947-960 gives a fixed path per logs folder (gateResultFile) and has GATE_WAIT_RULE report 'the gate did not finish' after MAX_GATE_WAITS=20 without stopping the gate. gates.json now sets parallelRepos 1, and the loop's own comment at :950 says a one-repo-at-a-time gate over five repos runs well past 1.5h. That makes a gate outrunning about 3h10m plausible. A later gate in the same folder (the ladder reruns into logs/<id>-ladder) can then get the leftover gate's envelope. Severity is below high: it needs a gate that runs past the full wait budget, and it needs the backgrounded Bash process to outlive the stage agent that started it, which I could not show for certain.
