findings.title: The gate can still tear down the run's own lease, and stackAfterLocal makes the window for it bigger
findings.what: None of the five commits changes takeLease or giveBack. acquireDecision still returns 'start' for the same holder when the stack is down, and runE2e still calls giveBack whenever lease.started. If a gate run under the run's holder finds the run's stack down, it starts the stack, then stops it and clears the run's lease. 0ff6e2f4 adds `if (context.stackAfterLocal) await context.localDone` before takeLease, and gates.json now sets stackAfterLocal true. The lease is therefore checked only after layer one, which with parallelRepos 1 can take well over an hour.
findings.scenario: The run holds the lease and the stack is up. During the ladder's 90-minute one-repo-at-a-time layer one, Docker Desktop restarts and the stack goes down. Before these commits the gate checked the lease when it started. Now it checks only after layer one. It finds its own holder with the stack down, starts the stack (started=true), runs E2E, then releases: it stops the stack and clears the run's lease. The next stage's lease status shows no lease and returns stackHeld with holder null, which stops the loop, or the run's own release at the end finds nothing to release.
findings.fix: In runE2e, when the holder is a build-run holder that already had a lease (the lease existed for this holder before acquire), never give it back: leave the stack up and the lease in place, and report startedForE2e so the loop knows. Or refuse with a 'stackDown' result so recoverDownStack takes the lease again properly. Add a gate.test case: a lease held by the same holder, the stack down, phase all. Assert that the lease file still names the holder and that stop-stack.sh was not called.
findings.verifierNote: stack-lease.js acquireDecision line 146: for the same holder, `if (!up) return 'start'`. acquireStack then calls startUnderLease (started:true), and gate.js:453 calls giveBack whenever lease.started, which stops the stack and clears the run's own lease. The bug is older than these commits and none of them changes it. gate.js:438 (`if (context.stackAfterLocal) await context.localDone`), together with gates.json stackAfterLocal true and parallelRepos 1, moves the lease check to after a long one-repo-at-a-time layer one, so the stack has more time to go down unseen. The likely outcome is that the loop stops on stackHeld with holder null. Code under test is not mistaken for green.

findings.title: Cross-service templates specs run on CDP, while the matching navigation specs are compose-only
findings.what: The INS templates-navigation, INS use-template and plants templates-navigation specs are tagged @compose. `npm test` (CDP) excludes them, following the precedent of address-book-navigation and cross-service-sessions. Every animals templates spec, though, crosses animals to INS (the type question) and back, and notification-type.spec crosses INS to animals and plants. None of those is tagged @compose, so they all run on CDP. Either the cross-service hop works on CDP, and three specs lose CDP coverage for no reason, or it does not, and about 60 templates and type-question tests will fail on CDP. Sam's rule is that a test behaves the same on both environments.
findings.scenario: A CDP run (`npm test`) executes create-template's beforeEach: Create new template leaves the animals origin for INS's /notification-type/template. If the cross-service session hop that keeps the navigation specs compose-only fails on CDP, every templates spec fails in beforeEach. If it works, the Templates and Use template links that start the templates flow from INS and plants are never checked on CDP.
findings.fix: Decide one way for the cross-service hop. Either remove @compose from the three navigation specs, since the templates specs show the hop is expected to work on CDP, or confirm on CDP that the hop fails and tag the templates and type-question specs to match. Record the reason either way.
findings.verifierNote: The tag split is inconsistent. The INS templates-navigation, INS use-template and plants templates-navigation specs (added in this merge, commits 17038b3 and b9adef9) are tagged @compose, so `npm test` (grep-invert '@compose') skips them on CDP. Meanwhile create-template, save-template, template-review and the other animals templates specs, the animals templates-navigation spec and notification-type.spec are tagged only @integration and make the same animals-to-INS or INS-to-animals/plants hop, using the same waitForURL-on-origin-change plus completeSignInIfRequested pattern. Neither the merge log nor the ruling gives a reason for the difference, and the existing precedent (address-book-navigation, cross-service-sessions) is also unexplained. One of the two groups is tagged wrongly for CDP.

findings.title: 'Listed first' assertions race with other workers saving templates as the same user
findings.what: Lines 68, 102 and 103 assert that the template this test just saved is the first card on Manage templates. Andrew's template list is shared by every worker, and Manage templates has no pagination, so it lists everything, newest first. Another worker's save that commits between this test's save and the Manage templates render takes first place. The 'Untitled template' case (line 103) is worse: several workers save untitled templates, so this test cannot tell which one is its own.
findings.scenario: Workers 2 and 5 press Save template within the same second. Worker 2's redirect renders after worker 5's save, so worker 5's card is first. firstCardViewLink's href holds worker 5's template id, and worker 2's test fails.
findings.fix: Run the save-template 'from a signed-in session' block as a dedicated cold identity, or assert the order relative to a template this test saved earlier, as the 'of two templates' test does. Also give names a crypto.randomUUID() suffix rather than Date.now() (save-template line 48, view-template line 54, template-review), as change-template and use-template already do. templateCard(name) uses exact matching, so a same-millisecond collision between workers breaks strict mode.
findings.verifierNote: save-template.spec.ts:68, 102 and 103 assert that the first card on Manage templates is this test's template, or that the first title is 'Untitled template'. Andrew's template list is shared by every parallel worker signed in as defaultUser, and several specs added in this merge save templates as Andrew. A save that commits between this test's save and the Manage templates render takes first place. For the untitled case, another worker's untitled save makes the test unable to tell which card is its own. The 'of two templates' test (124-137) uses relative order and is safe. The Date.now() name collision point is real but very unlikely. The main race holds.

findings.title: 'Never appears among the user's notifications' can never fail
findings.what: The test looks for the template's name on the dashboard. Dashboard cards show only a GBN-AG reference, commodity, origin, arrival, consignee, consignor and status, and none of these can hold a template name. So even if Save template wrongly created a draft notification, the name would still be absent and the assertion would pass.
findings.scenario: A regression makes saving a template also create a live-animals draft. The new draft appears first on Andrew's dashboard with a GBN-AG reference, getByText(name) still finds nothing, and the test stays green.
findings.fix: Record requests to the animals origin across the save, as create-template's requestsToAnimals does. Then assert none went to /live-animals/start or /live-animals/notifications/*. That holds up under parallel runs, unlike comparing the draft list (see F1). Alternatively, save as a dedicated cold identity and assert its dashboard has no drafts.
findings.verifierNote: save-template.spec.ts:139-146 asserts only that main contains no text matching the template name. In this merge the dashboard controller adds only a GET /start route. Dashboard cards render reference, commodity, origin, arrival, parties and status, and nothing carries a template name. findings.title: gate-wait cannot tell a dead gate from a slow one, so a crashed gate costs up to about 3 hours
findings.what: waitForGateResult only checks whether the result file exists. A gate killed by the OS or the tool (SIGKILL from memory pressure on the 16 GB laptop these commits are about, or a Bash tool that kills rather than backgrounds on timeout) writes no result. The catch block that writes an error envelope runs only for thrown errors, not for signals.
findings.scenario: A five-repo baseline's mvn verify and FIT suites push the laptop into memory pressure and the tim node process is killed. The agent gets GATE_STILL_RUNNING 20 times, about 3 hours, before reporting "the gate did not finish". Meanwhile no gate is running. If it was killed after the stack started, the stack is left up under the lease.
findings.fix: Have the gate write a marker with its pid when it starts (the same marker as GATE-1). Have gate-wait check that the pid is still alive (process.kill(pid, 0)) on each poll, and return a distinct GATE_DIED error at once when the process has gone and there is no result. Add a test that spawns a gate, kills it, and asserts that gate-wait reports it dead instead of still running.
findings.verifierNote: waitForGateResult only polls for the file. Nothing in gate-result.js or index.js records a pid or checks that the gate process is alive. The catch at index.js:343 runs only on thrown errors, so a SIGKILL of the tim node process writes nothing, and gate-wait answers GATE_STILL_RUNNING until the agent's 20 waits are used up. I rate it low: memory pressure is more likely to kill the large java or chromium children, which tim sees as a red rung, than the tim node parent. The loop's rule also moves a timed-out call to the background instead of killing it.

findings.title: Template updates are read-modify-write with a server-only version: a double-clicked Save returns 409 and two tabs silently overwrite each other
findings.what: updateDetails, replaceFulfilments and save each call load() (findByIdAndOwnerId), change the entity and then call repository.save(). @Version is on the entity, but the frontend client (services/templates/client.js) never sends the version back, and no endpoint accepts an expected version. The only concurrency check is whether two requests overlap inside the backend. Overlapping requests get an OptimisticLockingFailureException, which the global handler turns into 409 STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN. Requests that do not overlap silently overwrite each other, because PUT /fulfilments replaces the whole list.
findings.scenario: (a) The user double-clicks 'Save template' on the review page. Two POST /templates/{id}/save requests both load version 3. The first writes version 4. The second gets a 409, and the frontend's failed() throws a BackendRequestError, so the user sees an error page even though the template was saved. (b) The user opens a saved template in two tabs. Tab A changes origin, then tab B changes the consignee. Tab B's PUT /fulfilments sends the full answer list it read before A's change, so A's origin change is lost and no error is shown.
findings.fix: Make save idempotent and atomic. Use MongoTemplate.findAndModify with Criteria where(_id).is(id).and(ownerId).is(ownerId), and Update set(status, SAVED), so a repeated save is a no-op instead of a 409. Set 'saved' with a separate conditional update (criteria saved: null) or $min. For replaceFulfilments and updateDetails, accept the expected version (a concurrencyToken, as notifications use) and match on it, returning 409 when it is stale. Have the frontend send back the version it read and handle the 409 as notifications already do.
findings.verifierNote: Holds on the branch. NotificationTemplateService.save, replaceFulfilments and updateDetails all call load() and then repository.save() on an entity that carries @Version. The frontend client (services/templates/client.js) sends no version, and no endpoint accepts one. GlobalExceptionHandler maps OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409, and check-answers saveTemplate (controller.js:286) has no catch, so an overlapping save shows an error page. The template-records port sends the full fulfilment set it loaded earlier, so the two-tab lost update is real. Three things lower the severity. Notifications' own fulfilment replace has no expected-version check either (only /copy takes a concurrencyToken), so this copies the house pattern rather than falling short of it. A double-click gap (around 100ms) is usually longer than one Mongo find-and-save, so the second save normally runs after the first and leaves the template saved. And a lost update needs the same user editing in two tabs.

findings.title: GET /start creates a draft notification on any signed-in request (outside the conflict hunks, merged into the combined dashboard controller)
findings.what: `startGet` is registered on `GET /start` and runs `openNewNotification`. That calls `startJourney`, which creates and persists a draft through `records.create`, then `beginOpeningRun`. No crumb or confirmation step is involved. The backlog's own rule (c-309, restated in the notes of inc-157, inc-158 and inc-160) is that every state change is a form post. This route breaks that rule so that the INS type question can hand over cross-origin. Plants' dashboard gained the same route in the same merge.
findings.scenario: While signed in, a trader opens any page that links to /live-animals/start, or a link preview or prefetch fetches it. Lax cookies are sent on top-level GET navigation, so each fetch stores a new empty GBN-AG draft. The draft then appears on the dashboard and needs deleting.
findings.fix: Make /start idempotent and free of side effects. Render a GOV.UK confirmation page with its own crumb'd form post that creates the draft. Alternatively, have the INS type question hand over a short-lived signed token, and check it before creating anything. Apply the same change to plants' /start.
findings.verifierNote: The scenario holds. dashboard/controller.js:131-157 registers GET /start, which runs openNewNotification (startJourney followed by beginOpeningRun) and creates a draft with no crumb. The merge added this route (it is not in HEAD^1). The auth cookie is SameSite=Lax (config.js:19, auth.js:69), so a top-level cross-site GET or a prefetch carries the session and creates an empty draft. Two caveats lower the severity. First, it is a deliberate inc-148 design choice, documented in the code comment and backlog.json:182: a cross-origin POST cannot carry the crumb. It sat behind a human design gate (line 187). Second, the finding overstates c-309. In the backlog, c-309 covers storing and using templates through form posts, not every state change. The only impact is an unwanted empty draft, with no data exposure. This is not a merge-resolution defect, but it is real in the merged surface.

findings.title: Dead 'legacy row' handling and migration-style wording for null-status rows that cannot exist; such a row also bypasses the in-progress guard
findings.what: The whole template package arrives in this merge, and no environment has notification_templates rows. Even so, the Javadoc ('Rows written before templates could be created carry none and read as saved', 'or on a row saved before this was recorded') and the code (NotificationTemplateResponse.from treats a null status as SAVED, listFor's status-not-IN_PROGRESS filter lets null through, replaceFulfilments treats null as saved, and the sort orders by saved then created to place legacy rows) cater for rows from earlier increments on the same unmerged branch. That breaks the 'no migration comments' rule. It also means any row inserted without a status, for example by a raw seed or a future write path that forgets to set it, is listed and usable as a saved template.
findings.scenario: The IT seed() helper already inserts rows with no status, and they appear on Manage templates as saved. A future write path that builds a NotificationTemplate without .status(...) would quietly publish a half-made template to the user's list and let it start notifications.
findings.fix: Make status required: give it a @Builder.Default of IN_PROGRESS and drop the null branches. Have listFor query status == SAVED. Sort by saved descending only, or by (saved, _id). Remove the legacy wording from the Javadoc and the Schema descriptions, and make the IT seed() set status SAVED and saved explicitly.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. The whole template package is new in this merge (git log origin/main shows no history for it), and no seed in the tests repo or the frontend writes notification_templates, so no environment holds rows without a status. Even so, the NotificationTemplate Javadoc (lines 55-56 and 61-64) describes rows 'written before templates could be created' and 'saved before this was recorded'. The service Javadoc at line 17 says the same. NotificationTemplateResponse.from maps a null status to SAVED. The StatusNot(IN_PROGRESS) query lets a null status through, and the IT findAll_shouldStillListARowWithNoStatus seeds a 'Legacy' row to pin that behaviour. This is migration-style wording and handling, which the house rules ban. It also means a row written without a status shows up in the list as a saved template.

findings.title: GET /templates is unbounded and returns every template's full answers
findings.what: listFor loads every saved template for the owner, with no limit or paging. Each NotificationTemplateSummary carries the complete fulfilments list, which is the whole notification answer payload, so the frontend can summarise cards. Nothing limits the number of templates per user or the size of the fulfilments.
findings.scenario: A high-volume importer keeps 200 templates, each holding a full set of commodity, party and transport answers. Every visit to Manage templates pulls all 200 documents and serialises them into one response, which the frontend then decodes. Latency and heap use grow linearly, and a large account can push the backend toward OOM under concurrent load.
findings.fix: Add paging, as notifications already have (page and size, plus totalItems from count). Alternatively, project only the fields the card needs (category, parties' addresses) on the server rather than returning the raw fulfilments. Consider a per-user cap on templates.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. listFor calls findAllByOwnerIdAndStatusNotOrderBySavedDescCreatedDesc with no Pageable and no limit. NotificationTemplateSummary carries the full fulfilments, and the frontend Manage templates page decodes every one through cardAnswersFor. Notifications have paging and templates do not. The impact is speculative at expected per-user volumes, so the severity is low.

findings.title: POST /templates/{id}/save is an action path, not a noun endpoint

findings.title: Germinal hand-off test pins the /start URL and passes on a 404
findings.what: The animals frontend has no /germinal-products route yet. The ruling (inc-148 gate) allows the link to land before the set exists, so today the test passes on a 404 page. It checks only the landed pathname, with a non-retrying expect. When the germinal set is built and /start creates a draft and redirects to its first page, the landed path will no longer be /start, and the test will fail even though the hand-off works.
findings.scenario: The germinal theme ships GET /germinal-products/start, which creates a draft and redirects to /germinal-products/notifications/<id>/origin. continueToService resolves on the final URL, so the toBe(`/germinal-products/start`) check fails.
findings.fix: Capture the hand-off request instead: wait for a request whose pathname is `${SET_BASES.germinalProducts}/start` on the animals origin. Keep the check that no /live-animals/ request was made. Do this before the germinal set lands, so the test holds up when it does.
findings.verifierNote: No germinal route exists in the animals frontend source (grep finds only copy and test references), so today the hand-off lands on a 404 and notification-type.spec.ts:158-160 passes on the URL alone, with plain non-retrying expects. continueToService waits only for the origin change and then for load, so the URL read is the final one after any redirect. The live-animals precedent in this merge (dashboard startGet) creates a draft and redirects to the origin page. When germinal follows that shape, the toBe('/germinal-products/start') check will fail even though the hand-off works. This is brittle but correct today, so the severity is low.

findings.title: GET /start creates a notification draft in animals and plants, against the 'every state change is a form post' ruling
findings.what: startGet (in the animals frontend and in the plants dashboard controller) creates a draft, adds it to the known-journeys cookie and begins the opening run on a plain GET, with no crumb or hand-off token. The 9 October afternoon ruling (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm.md:199) says every state change is a form post. A GET with side effects is also triggered by things that never meant to create anything.
findings.scenario: Several things each mint a new empty draft in the trader's list: a link to <animals>/live-animals/start from any site (top-level navigation carries the Lax or Strict same-site session cookie within cdp-int.defra.cloud), browser prefetch or prerender of a typed or suggested URL, a link-preview bot running in the user's session, and a refresh of /start. inc-148's own AC says abandoning the question leaves no empty draft, which these paths break.
findings.fix: Have INS hand over with a short-lived signed hand-off token, as the address-book handshake does: INS mints an HMAC'd nonce, and /start creates the draft only when the token verifies and has not been used. Or make /start render a one-button, crumb-protected 'Continue' form that POSTs to the existing create route. Either way, an unauthenticated-intent GET no longer writes.
findings.verifierNote: Holds. The merge added startGet (animals dashboard/controller.js:131-132), which on a plain GET with no crumb or token calls startJourney and beginOpeningRun, the same as createPost. That is deliberate: a comment says a cross-origin POST cannot carry the crumb. A top-level navigation, a refresh, or a prerender of /start each creates a new empty draft owned by the signed-in trader. That goes against the backlog AC that the question leaves no stray draft. The 9 Oct pm ruling's 'every state change is a form post' is mainly about working without JavaScript, but it still applies. The impact is nuisance drafts, not a data leak or a privilege problem, so I rated it low.

findings.title: No template-mode page is ever audited by Lighthouse
findings.what: audit-targets builds its targets from features/index.js allRoutes. The template-mode twins (/templates/{journeyId}, which is the template task list and the saved template page, and every /templates/{journeyId}/<slug>) are generated only in routes-live-animals.js by templateModeRoutes, so they are neither audited nor listed in SKIPPED. The 'stale reason fails the build' guard cannot see them either.
findings.scenario: An accessibility regression on the saved template page or the template review, such as a duplicate h1, an unlabelled Change link or the 'Template' strip, passes the Lighthouse gate, because only /templates, /templates/new and the notification pages are audited.
findings.fix: Feed auditPaths the same route list the server registers: allRoutes plus templateModeRoutes(allRoutes, {excludedSlugs}). Seed a saved template and an in-progress template in the Lighthouse setup, and map /templates/{journeyId}/* to those ids (a FILLED_BY-style map keyed to 'template'). Twins that are not worth auditing go into SKIPPED with reasons.
findings.verifierNote: Holds. scripts/lighthouse/audit-targets.js builds auditPaths and assertTargetsAreCurrent from allRoutes (features/index.js). allRoutes includes the templates controller's own routes (/templates, /templates/new, and /templates/{journeyId}/name in SKIPPED), but not the twins. Those are generated only in routes-live-animals.js:136-140 through templateModeRoutes. So the saved-template page, the template task list and every template-mode page twin are neither audited nor listed in SKIPPED, and the stale-skip guard cannot see them.

findings.title: Template unit tests spy on internal modules and one expectation is computed by the code under test
findings.what: use-template.test.js stubs templates.getFor, engine/journey.startJourney and flow/run-state.beginOpeningRun with vi.spyOn. It then asserts `startJourney` toHaveBeenCalledWith `{ fulfilment: notificationSeedFrom(decoded) }`, so the expected value comes from the production function itself. The same pattern appears elsewhere. controller.test.js:62 spies templates.listFor and :128 spies countries.originDisplayLabel. check-answers.test.js (template review block) spies templates.saveFor, reads the session through the production helper takeSavedTemplate, and controller.test.js:225 asserts on the raw session key 'templateSaved'. None of these are network-boundary mocks, even though the templates service has a stub mode and an HTTP client that nock could intercept.
findings.scenario: A regression in notificationSeedFrom (for example, the arrival date no longer stripped) changes both sides of the use-template assertion, so the test stays green. Renaming the session key or moving startJourney's signature breaks tests while behaviour is unchanged.
findings.fix: Run these handlers against the templates stub (or nock the backend in real mode) and the in-memory store. Assert the resulting draft's stored answers and the redirect, not the calls to internal functions. For the banner, assert that the next GET /templates renders the heading, not the session contents.
findings.verifierNote: The spies are real: use-template.test.js:61-65 (templates.getFor, journey.startJourney, runState.beginOpeningRun), controller.test.js:62/128/232 (templates.listFor, countries.originDisplayLabel), the raw 'templateSaved' session key at controller.test.js:175-225, and check-answers.test.js:2811/2828 (templates.saveFor). use-template.test.js:86-88 does build its expected value with notificationSeedFrom. The claimed impact is smaller than stated, though. Line 90 also asserts a concrete value ('further-keeping'), seed-notification.test.js tests notificationSeedFrom directly, and use-template.fit.spec.js drives the real UI. So a seeding regression would not go unnoticed. What remains is a house-rule breach (mocks below the network boundary) in a codebase that already does this in places, for example check-answers.test.js:488 spying on records.load before the merge.

findings.title: Saved banner is taken from the session before the cards are built
findings.what: takeSavedTemplate clears the session key at line 60. `Promise.all(saved.map(toCard))` runs afterwards at line 70, and it awaits countries.originDisplayLabel, which loads reference data. The comment above line 60 claims the banner survives a failed render, but that only holds for a failed list call.
findings.scenario: A user saves a template and is redirected to Manage templates. The list call succeeds, but the countries reference data fails to load on a cold cache, so the page errors. The banner has already been cleared, so on the next visit the user never sees the 'saved to templates' confirmation.
findings.fix: Build templateCards before calling takeSavedTemplate (or take it last, just before h.view). Then drop the comment, because the ordering shows the intent.
findings.verifierNote: controller.js:60 calls takeSavedTemplate, which runs yar.clear, before line 70 awaits Promise.all(saved.map(toCard)). toCard goes through cardAnswersFor and then countries.originDisplayLabel, and ensureLoaded throws Boom.serverUnavailable outside stub mode when reference data fails to load. yar still saves the cleared session on an error response, so the one-time banner is lost. The comment at lines 58-59 only covers the list call failing. This needs a real-mode reference-data failure at the exact moment after a save, so it is low.
